name: Spring Turkey
dof_breakdown: actuated hip and knee on each leg; roll, yaw and lateral motion constrained by a boom
summary: Designed and built by Peter Dilworth and Jerry Pratt in 1994, Spring Turkey marked the Leg Lab's turn from hydraulics to force-controlled electric drive. All its motors sit in the upper body and reach the joints through cable drives, with a spring deliberately placed in series at every degree of freedom — the arrangement that became known as the Series Elastic Actuator. It walked at about 0.5 m/s and was retired in 1996 after mechanical trouble, replaced by Spring Flamingo.
notable: First robot built around Series Elastic Actuators — a spring in series with every motor
Test bed for Virtual Model Control
~12 Nm at the hips, ~18 Nm at the knees, ~20 Hz force-control bandwidth
